touches.text: A ticket's code is a tool or machine; its life is data. All of its state is on disk, so anyone can instantiate it to talk to it, and any dialog is written to the relevant part of the ticket as it happens. To cross a gate the ticket asks that gate to queue it, sending only its fileref: devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>. The gate instantiates the ticket from that fileref on its own side. A ticket instance then processes the pass or fail: on a pass it goes on to the next step, alerting the probes watching the gate (3.3.4.2); on a fail it asks design to queue it, the same way. Self-queuing is the abstract ticket's (3.3.2), so every kind inherits it and no caller queues a ticket on its behalf. WHY: encapsulation. The ticket crosses as a fileref and the other side builds its own instance, so nothing is shared across the boundary but the address.
Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work.

More than one builder works on one box, and there will be more than two, so the whole-tree rule (a PROVEME crossing refuses while anything in either tree is uncommitted, working_tree_clean) is re-examined for N builders on a box. One builder's work must not block another's crossing.
The crossing is the ticket's own act. The gate's probe (the same kind that sends notice of gate passage) tells the passing ticket "you can now advance to X", and the ticket updates itself.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:
charter: compiles a component's bounded state from its history. WHY: state is compiled from the component's tickets, never hand-edited (Law 5). Held by CodeMother.
